name: Landmine Meadows Rear Delt Flye
description: The landmine Meadows rear delt flye uses the bar end of a landmine setup and a staggered stance to perform a rear delt fly with a fixed arc of motion determined by the pivot of the barbell. Unlike dumbbell reverse flyes, the landmine provides a constant and smoothly changing resistance curve, and the bar's weight progression is more granular, making it excellent for systematically building rear deltoid strength.

execution.starting_position: Secure a barbell in a landmine unit. Stand perpendicular to the bar in a staggered stance, hinge forward at the hips. Grasp the bar end with one hand, arm hanging below the shoulder.
execution.setup_instructions: Hinge to approximately 45-70 degrees forward so the bar end hangs naturally. Use lighter loading than a Meadows row — rear delts are smaller than lats.
steps: Step 1: Begin hinged with bar end hanging in the working hand.
Step 2: Raise the working arm out to the side in a lateral arc, keeping the elbow slightly bent.
Step 3: Continue raising until the arm is at shoulder height.
Step 5: Lower under control back to the hanging position.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbow too much — this becomes a row, not a fly
Excessive torso rotation to assist the raise
safety_considerations: Light loads — rear delt is a small muscle group
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arm hanging to shoulder height lateral position.
coaching_cues: Lead with the elbow — slight bend throughout
Think of pulling the arm upward like opening a wing
Feel the back of the shoulder contract at the top
